meta.title: Directive (EU) 2016/343 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 9 March 2016 on the strengthening of certain aspects of the presumption of innocence and of the right to be present at the trial in criminal proceedings

items.heading: CHAPTER 1

items.text: This Directive lays down common minimum rules concerning:
items.heading: Article 1
items.comment: As this Article only describes the scope of the Directive in terms of content, a transposition does not seem to be required. Because the individual safeguards are largely guaranteed under German law without explicit implementation, de facto / indirect implementation was assumed.

items.text:
(a)

certain aspects of the presumption of innocence in criminal proceedings;
items.comment:
With the exception of Art. 6 (2) of the ECHR, which takes on the status of a simple law ("einfaches Gesetz") in German law (for further details see the commentary on Art. 3 (1) - Art. 6 (2) ECHR), the guarantees summarised under this generic term are not explicitly laid down in German law. However, they are derived from the constitution and are presupposed in several provisions, particularly in the Code of Criminal Procedure (for further details, see below). The national legislator therefore saw no need for implementation (legislative materials to the Act to Strengthen the Right of the Accused to Be Present at the Trial, BR-Drucks. 384/18, pp. 9 et seqq, BT-Drucks. 19/446, p. 9).

As a result the details of these warranties are not explicitly specified. This has several disadvantages: Beyond the obvious essence of the guarantee, it might make the individual specifications appear less susceptible to change. Moreover, it could give rise to the risk that the addressees of the guarantees are not sufficiently aware of the requirements to be observed in their particular situation. However, the warranties in the Directive are also the core area of warranties in national law as also recognised in practice.

Since no statutory text can be referred to that would illustrate the content of the respective warranties in German law, its basic outlines are described in more detail in the commentaries.

items.text:
(b)

the right to be present at the trial in criminal proceedings.
items.comment: In order to adapt German law to the requirements of Article 8 of the Directive regarding the right to be present in criminal proceedings, the Act to Strengthen the Right of the Accused to Be Present at the Trial ("Gesetz zur Stärkung des Rechts des Angeklagten auf Anwesenheit in der Verhandlung", BGBl I 2018, p. 2571, in force since 21 December 2018) was adopted. The changes to the previously applicable law were minor and therefore de facto/implicit transposition was assumed. For further details see the commentary on Art. 8 of the Directive.

items.text: This Directive applies to natural persons who are suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings. It applies at all stages of the criminal proceedings, from the moment when a person is suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence, or an alleged criminal offence, until the decision on the final determination of whether that person has committed the criminal offence concerned has become definitive.
items.heading: Article 2
items.comment:
It is recognised that the presumption of innocence applies until the guilt is finally established (instead of many Meyer-Goßner/Schmitt, StPO, 62nd ed. 2019, EMRK Art. 6 para 12).

The right to be present is comprehensively recognised in German law for the factual instances (first instance and appellate instance ["Berufungsinstanz"]). For the instance, which decides on appeal on points of law ("Revisionsinstanz), this can only be assumed to a limited extent, as the provision on the presence of the accused in custody in section 350 (2) 2 CCP shows. For further details see the commentary on Art. 8 (1).

items.heading: CHAPTER 2

items.text: Member States shall ensure that suspects and accused persons are presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law.
items.heading: Article 3

provisions.textEn: The legislature shall be bound by the constitutional order, the executive and the judiciary by law and justice.

provisions.comment:
As a result of its transformation into German law, the guarantees of the ECHR have the status of an ordinary statute. According to the settled case-law of the Federal Constitutional Court, however, they influence the interpretation of the fundamental rights and constitutional principles of the Basic Law. The text of the ECHR Convention and the case-law of the ECtHR serve as interpretative aids for determining the content and scope of fundamental rights and constitutional principles of the Basic Law.

Thus, within the framework of a methodology-based interpretation, German courts must give priority to an interpretation that is in line with the Convention. They must also take account of the relevant case-law of the ECtHR, i.e. they must take note of it, include it in the decision-making process and consider it appropriately.

(For further details, see the key decision of the Federal Constitutional Court BVerfGE 111, 307 et seqq - Görgülü).
provisions.textEn: Everyone charged with a criminal offence shall be presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law.

items.comment:
In German law, the presumption of innocence is explicitly laid down not in the CCP, but in Article 6 (2) of the ECHR, which, due to its transformation, has the rank of an ordinary statute ("einfaches Gesetz"). It is also guaranteed under constitutional law and is thus derived from the principle of the rule of law in Article 20 (3) of the Basic Law ("Grundgesetz") (BVerfGE 19, 342, 347 f.; 35, 311, 320; 74, 358, 369 ff.; 74, 358, 370; 82, 106, 118 ff.; 110, 1, 22 f.; 111, 307, 323 f.). The suspect's innocence is presumed until the legal proof of his guilt is established and he is thus protected against disadvantages that amount to a verdict of guilty or a sentence without his guilt having been established beforehand in proceedings in accordance with the law. Or, as the Federal Constitutional Court ("Bundesverfassungsgericht") states, the presumption of innocence prohibits, in actual criminal proceedings, the imposition of measures on the accused which have the effect of imposing a penalty and treating the accused as guilty in procedural terms, without proof of guilt being established according to the the rules of procedure; it also requires proof of guilt to be established in a final judgment before it can be generally invoked against the accused in legal proceedings (BVerfGE 35, 311, 320; 74, 358, 369 f.). In determining the content and scope of the constitutional presumption of innocence, the Federal Constitutional Court, as an interpretative aid, also draws on the content of Art. 6 (2) ECHR and the relevant case-law of the ECtHR (BVerfGE 74, 358, 370; 111, 307, 322 et seqq).


The disadvantages of the absence of a more detailed stipulation see the commentary on Art. 1 (a) of the Directive.

items.heading: Article 4

items.text: 1. Member States shall take the necessary measures to ensure that, for as long as a suspect or an accused person has not been proved guilty according to law, public statements made by public authorities, and judicial decisions, other than those on guilt, do not refer to that person as being guilty. This shall be without prejudice to acts of the prosecution which aim to prove the guilt of the suspect or accused person, and to preliminary decisions of a procedural nature, which are taken by judicial or other competent authorities and which are based on suspicion or incriminating evidence.

nationalActs.title: Richtlinien für das Strafverfahren und das Bußgeldverfahren
nationalActs.titleEn: Directives on criminal and administrative fine proceedings

provisions.textEn:
No unnecessary exposure of the accused

The public prosecutor avoids anything that could lead to an exposure of the accused that is not required by the purpose of the investigation. This applies in particular to correspondence with other authorities and persons. If the name of the accused or the crime he is accused of is not dispensable, it must be made clear that the accused is merely suspected of a crime.

items.comment:
The essence of the presumption of innocence in its formulation by the Federal Constitutional Court ("Bundesverfassungsgericht") concerns the treatment of the accused in criminal proceedings and therefore the content of sentence 1, alternative 2 - the statement as guilty in a judicial decision without determination of guilt (see for example the decision by the Federal Constitutional Court BVerfGE 74, 358 et seqq. in the case law section). But it must also be taken into account by the other public authorities. The presumption of innocence therefore in accordance with Art. 4 (1) 1 alt. 1 forbids statements by a public official concerning a person accused of a crime, that reflect the view that he or she is guilty before legal proof of guilt has been established (BGH, 1 StR 154/16, judgement of 7/09/2016). The same results from Art. 6 (2) ECHR, as is apparent inter alia from the judgment of the ECtHR - El Kaada v. Germany (application-no. 2130/10), judgment of 12/11/2015, para 53 (as mentioned on the case law section; regarding the applicability of the ECHR in German law see the commentary on Art. 3 (1) - Art. 6 (2) ECHR).

For the public prosecutor, this obligation arises further from No. 4a Directives on criminal and administrative fine proceedings (Richtlinien für das Strafverfahren und das Bußgeldverfahren, RiStBV). However, the RiStBV are administrative regulations without legal force. They are issued by the Federal Ministry of Justice and Consumer Protection, are primarily aimed at the public prosecutor's office and the police and are intended to ensure a uniform approach in the relevant procedures.

The federal legal provisions governing the press' rights to information against the prosecuting authorities require the latter to weigh up conflicting interests. In doing so, they must take into account the presumption of innocence. If they decide to make a declaration on this basis, they must always state clearly that so far only the suspicion of a criminal offence exists (legislative materials, BR-Drucks. 384/18, S. 9).

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that appropriate measures are available in the event of a breach of the obligation laid down in paragraph 1 of this Article not to refer to suspects or accused persons as being guilty, in accordance with this Directive and, in particular, with Article 10.

provisions.textEn:
Challenge of judge; fear of bias

(1) A judge may be challenged both where he has been barred by law from exercising judicial office and for fear of bias.

(2) A challenge for fear of bias may be brought where there is reason to doubt the impartiality of a judge.

(3) The public prosecution office, the private prosecutor and the accused may exercise the right of challenge. The court personnel appointed to participate in the decision shall be named upon the request of the parties entitled to exercise the right of challenge.

Admissibility

An appeal on points of law shall be admissible against judgments of the criminal divisions, of the criminal divisions with lay judges and against judgments of the higher regional courts pronounced at first instance.

Grounds for appeal on points of law

(1) An appeal on points of law may be filed only on the ground that the judgment was based on a violation of the law.

(2) Failure to apply a legal norm or erroneous application of a legal norm shall constitute a violation of the law.

Absolute grounds for appeal on points of law

A judgment shall always be considered to be based on a violation of the law

[...]

3.  if a professional judge or a lay judge participated in reaching the judgment after he was challenged for bias and the motion for challenge was either declared to be well-founded or erroneously rejected;

[...].

items.comment:
Where a judicial decision violates the presumption of innocence, the accused may challenge it on the regular legal remedies: Judgements with the appeal according to sections 312 et seqq CCP and the appeal on points of law according to sections 333 et seqq CCP, other court decisions with the appeal according to section 304 CCP, if this is not excluded according to section 305 CCP.

However, according to section 337 CCP, a successful appeal on points of law requires in principle that the judgment is based on the violation of law. It must therefore be possible that the judgment would have been different without the violation of the presumption of innocence. The main conceivable effect could be on the level of sentences. In recent years, the Federal Court of Justice has increasingly begun to compensate for the violation of procedural rights by considering part of the sentence as already executed. For violations of the presumption of innocence, it has explicitly refused to do so; on the other hand, it has left open whether the disadvantages suffered as a result must be taken into account in the context of the regular assessment of the penalty under section 46 CC (BGH NJW 2016, 3670; in favour, for example, Meyer-Goßner/Schmitt, StPO, 62nd ed. 2019, ECHR Article 6 para. 15b).


If a statement made by a deciding judge during or outside the hearing violates the presumption of innocence, this is a reason to doubt his impartiality in accordance with section 24 (2) CCP. The accused can therefore challenge the judge pursuant to section 24 (1) CCP for fear of bias. If the judge participated in reaching the judgment despite the challenging and the motion for challenge was either declared to be well-founded or erroneously rejected, the accused can lodge an appeal on points of law. This violation of the law is a so-called absolute ground for appeal, so that according to section 338 No. 2 CCP it is legally presumed that the judgment is based on it.

However, the rules on impartiality in sections 22 CCP apply only to judges and are therefore, according to the prevailing opinion including that of the Federal Court of Justice, not applicable to the public prosecutor. Therefore, if the public prosecutor in a statement violates the presumption of innocence, the accused can only suggest a replacement to his hierarchical superiors. If the public prosecutor nevertheless remains in the proceedings, this could impair their fairness and in this respect also justify an appeal on points of law. In this case, however, the judgment would have to be based on the infringement.


If public communications by courts and authorities violate the presumption of innocence, the person concerned can take action before the administrative courts (BGH, 2 ArS 188/15, decision of 27/7/2017). He/she may also claim damages from official liability accordning to section 839 of the German Civil Code (legislative materials, BR-Drucks. 384/18).

items.text: 3. The obligation laid down in paragraph 1 not to refer to suspects or accused persons as being guilty shall not prevent public authorities from publicly disseminating information on the criminal proceedings where strictly necessary for reasons relating to the criminal investigation or to the public interest.

provisions.textEn:
Alert for arrest

(1) The judge or the public prosecution office and, in exigent circumstances, its investigators (section 152 of the Courts Constitution Act) may issue an alert for arrest on the basis of a warrant for arrest or an order for placement.

(2) If the conditions are met for a warrant of arrest or an order for placement the issuance of which cannot be awaited without endangering the success of the investigations, the public prosecution office and its investigators (section 152 of the Courts Constitution Act) may order measures under subsection (1) if this is necessary for a provisional arrest. The decision on the issuance of a warrant of arrest or an order for placement shall be obtained without delay and at the latest within one week.

(3) In the case of an offence of substantial significance, the judge and the public prosecution office may, in the cases under subsections (1) and (2), also order public searches if other means of determining the accused’s whereabouts would offer much less prospect of success or would be much more difficult. In exigent circumstances and if the judge or the public prosecution office cannot be reached in time, the public prosecution office’s investigators (section 152 of the Courts Constitution Act) shall also be entitled to exercise this power, subject to the same conditions. In the cases under sentence 2, the decision of the public prosecution office shall be obtained without delay. The order shall become ineffective if it is not confirmed within 24 hours.

(4) The accused shall be named and, where necessary, described as accurately as possible; an image may be attached. The offence of which he is suspected, the place and time of its commission, as well as circumstances which may be relevant for his apprehension may be indicated.

(5) Sections 115 and 115a shall apply accordingly.

Alert to determine whereabouts

(1) An alert may be issued requiring determination of the whereabouts of an accused or of a witness if his whereabouts are not known.

(2) Subsection (1) shall also apply to alerts referring to the accused insofar as they are necessary to secure a driving licence, to carry out identification measures, to conduct a DNA analysis or to establish his identity.

(3) A public search may also be ordered in the case of an offence of substantial significance on the basis of an alert requiring determination of the whereabouts of an accused or of a witness if the accused is strongly suspected of having committed the offence and where other means of determining his whereabouts would offer much less prospect of success or would be much more difficult.

(4) Section 131 (4) shall apply accordingly. When determining the whereabouts of a witness it shall be made clear that the person sought is not the accused. There shall be no public search if overriding interests of the witness meriting protection present an obstacle thereto. Images of the witness may be used only if other means of determining his whereabouts would offer no prospect of success or would be much more difficult.

(5) The alerts referred to in subsections (1) and (2) may be issued in all search instruments used by the prosecuting authorities.

provisions.comment:
Under strict conditions, sections 131 et seqq. CCP allow for public searches and the publication of images of a suspect for investigative reasons. In particular, the offence of which the suspect is suspected must be substantial significance and other means muss offer much less prospect of success or must be much more difficult. Thus, as required by recital 18, the use of these investigative measures is confined to situations in which it is reasonable and proportionate, also since the measures, like any infringement of fundamental rights, are subject to the general principle of proportionality.

Further specifications of the prerequisites and implementation are contained in the Directives on the use of publication organs and the use of the Internet as well as other electronic means of communication for the public search for persons in criminal proceedings ("Richtlinien über die Inanspruchnahme von Publikationsorganen und die Nutzung des Internets sowie anderer elektronischer Kommunikationsmittel zur Öffentlichkeitsfahndung nach Personen im Rahmen von Strafverfahren") as Annex B to the Directives on criminal and administrative fine proceedings ("Richtlinien für das Strafverfahren und das Bußgeldverfahren, RiStBV"). The RiStBV are administrative regulations without legal force. They are issued by the Federal Ministry of Justice and Consumer Protection, are primarily aimed at the public prosecutor's office and the police and are intended to ensure a uniform approach in the relevant procedures.
provisions.textEn:
Publication of images of accused or witness

(1) Publication of images of an accused who is suspected of having committed an offence of substantial significance shall also be admissible if investigating an offence, in particular establishing the identity of an unknown offender, by other means would offer much less prospect of success or would be much more difficult.

(2) Publication of images of a witness and references to the criminal proceedings underlying such publication shall also be admissible if investigating an offence of substantial significance, in particular establishing the identity of the witness, by other means would offer no prospect of success or would be much more difficult. The publication must make it clear that the person in the image is not an accused person.

(3) Section 131 (4) sentence 1 half-sentence 1 and sentence 2 shall apply accordingly.

Provision of information to and inspection of files by private individuals and other agencies

(1) Without prejudice to the provision of section 406e, a lawyer may obtain information from a file for a private individual or for other agencies if such file is available to the court or would have to be submitted to the court if public charges were preferred and if he sets forth a legitimate interest therefor. Information shall be refused if the data subject has an interest meriting protection in such refusal.

(2) Inspection of the files may be granted under the conditions of subsection (1) if the provision of information would require disproportionate effort or if it would be insufficient to exercise the justifiable interest according to the explanation supplied by the person requesting inspection of the files.

(3) Items of evidence in official custody may be viewed under the conditions of subsection (2).

(4) Private persons and other agencies may also be given information from the files under the conditions of subsection (1).

provisions.comment: Publicity of the trial was originally admitted for the purpose of judicial control, but now mainly for the information of the general public. Publicity means only the direct publicity of the persons present in the courtroom and the indirect publicity through their report. Records and transmissions of the hearing are in principle prohibited (subsection 1 2), except for sound transmission to a so-called media workroom ((subsection 1 3) as well as the transmission and recording of pronouncements of decisions of the Federal Court of Justice (subsection) and the Federal Constitutional Court (section 17a Federal Constitutional Court Act - BVerfGG). Audio recordings of hearings, including the pronouncement of judgements and rulings, may be authorised by the court for academic or historical purposes according to subsection 2.
provisions.textEn:
Section 169

(1) Hearings before the adjudicating court, including the pronouncement of judgments and rulings, shall be public. Audio and television or radio recordings as well as audio and film recordings intended for public presentation or for publication of their content shall be inadmissible. Audio transmissions to a workspace for persons reporting for the press, radio, television or other media may be authorised by the court. Audio transmissions may, in part, be prohibited in order to protect the legitimate interests of the parties or of third parties or to ensure the proper course of proceedings. In all other respects, sentence 2 shall apply to audio transmission to a workspace accordingly.

(2) Audio recordings of hearings, including the pronouncement of judgements and rulings, may be authorised by the court for academic or historical purposes if the relevant proceedings are of paramount significance for the contemporary history of the Federal Republic of Germany. In order to protect the legitimate interests of the parties or of third parties and to ensure the proper course of proceedings, the making of such recordings may, in part, be prohibited. The recordings shall not be included in the files of the proceedings and may not be disclosed, nor may they be used or reviewed for purposes of the recorded or other proceedings. Upon the conclusion of the proceedings, the court shall offer to transfer the recordings to the competent Federal Archives or Land Archive; the Federal Archives or Land Archive must determine, in accordance with the Federal Archives Act or a Land Archive Act, whether the recordings are of lasting value. If the Federal Archives or the respective Land Archive do not accept the recordings, the Court shall delete the recordings.

(3) By way of derogation from section 1 sentence 2, the Court may admit audio and television or radio recordings as well as audio and film recordings intended for public presentation or for publication of their content for the pronouncement of decisions of the Federal Court of Justice in special cases. In order to protect the legitimate interest of the parties or of third parties and to ensure the proper course of proceedings, the making or transmission of recordings may be prohibited in part or further conditions may be attached thereto.

(4) The court’s rulings in accordance with paragraphs 1 to 3 are incontestable.

§ 4 Right of the press to information

(1) The authorities are obliged to provide information to representatives of the press who identify themselves as such in order to fulfil their public duties.

(2) Information may only be refused insofar as

1.    provisions on secrecy stand in the way, or

2.    measures must by their nature be kept secret, whether permanently or temporarily, because their disclosure or premature disclosure would harm or jeopardise the public interest, or

3.   this could frustrate, impede, delay or endanger the proper conduct of a pending proceeding, or

4. a private interest worthy of protection would be violated.

(3) General orders prohibiting an authority from providing information to the press are inadmissible.


(4) The publishers of a newspaper or magazine may require the authorities to ensure that their official announcements are not sent to them for use later than to their competitors.

provisions.textEn:
23 Cooperation with press and broadcasting services

(1) When informing the public, cooperation shall be established with the press, radio and television, taking into account their specific functions and their importance for the formation of public opinion. Such information shall not jeopardise the purpose of the investigation or prejudge the outcome of the trial and shall not prejudice the accused's right to a fair trial. It must also be examined in each individual case whether the public interest in full reporting outweighs the personal rights of the accused or other parties involved, in particular the injured party. An unnecessary exposure of this person is to be avoided. It will generally be possible to satisfy the general interest of the public in information without mentioning names. Reference is made to No. 129 para. 1, No. 219 para. 1. The relevant administrative regulations of the Länder must be observed (see also Annex B ).

(2) The public may in principle only be informed about the indictment and details of the indictment after the bill of indictment has been served on the accused or otherwise made public.

Reporting by press and radio

(1) The press, radio and television may not be restricted in their reporting beyond what is required by law and the purpose of the trial. The task of the court to investigate the truth must not be thwarted or made more difficult, nor must the right of the accused to defend himself unhindered be impaired; the personal rights of the accused and other parties involved, in particular of the injured party, must also be taken into account (cf. no. 23).

(2) During the main hearing, including the pronouncement of the judgment, sound and television broadcast recordings as well as sound and film recordings for the purpose of public presentation or publication of their contents are not permitted.

(3) The chairman shall decide whether and under what conditions sound, film and image recordings may otherwise be made in the courtroom.

(4) The holder of the domiciliary rights shall decide on the admissibility of sound, film and image recordings in the Court building outside the courtroom.

items.comment:
German Law allows the public dissemination of information on the criminal proceedings for both purposes mentioned in the Directive.

  • Sections 131 et seqq. CCP allow for investigative measures explicitly addressed to the public.
  • Section 169 CCA regulates the publicity of the main trial.
  • Also, the media have a right to information against the criminal prosecution authorities, although it is disputed whether this arises from section 475 CCP or the respective state press law, such as section 4 Federal State Press Law Berlin. However, these provisions are very general. No. 23, 129 of the Directives on criminal and administrative fine proceedings (Richtlinien für das Strafverfahren und das Bußgeldverfahren, RiStBV). The RiStBV are administrative regulations without legal force. They are issued by the Federal Ministry of Justice and Consumer Protection, are primarily aimed at the public prosecutor's office and the police and are intended to ensure a uniform approach in the relevant procedures.

items.heading: Article 5
items.subHeading: Presentation of suspects and accused persons

items.text: 1. Member States shall take appropriate measures to ensure that suspects and accused persons are not presented as being guilty, in court or in public, through the use of measures of physical restraint.
